[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Vision Transformers (ViT) and Swin Transformers"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Introduction to Vision Transformers (ViT)"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Vision Transformer (ViT) applies the standard Transformer architecture directly to images with minimal modifications. While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) rely on inductive biases like translation invariance and locality, ViT treats image patches as visual tokens analogous to words in natural language processing."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Core Architecture of ViT"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Patch Extraction: An image of size H x W x C is reshaped into a sequence of flattened 2D patches of size P x P."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Linear Projection: Patches are mapped to a latent vector dimension D using a trainable linear layer."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Position Embeddings: Standard 1D learnable position embeddings are added to the patch embeddings to retain spatial awareness."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Transformer Encoder: Consists of alternating layers of Multi-Head Self-Attention (MSA) and Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP)."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Implementing ViT Patch Embedding in PyTorch"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class PatchEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, img_size=224, patch_size=16, in_channels=3, embed_dim=768):
        super().__init__()
        self.img_size = img_size
        self.patch_size = patch_size
        self.n_patches = (img_size // patch_size) ** 2
        
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(
            in_channels,
            embed_dim,
            kernel_size=patch_size,
            stride=patch_size
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        # x shape: (batch_size, in_channels, img_size, img_size)
        x = self.proj(x)  # (batch_size, embed_dim, h_patches, w_patches)
        x = x.flatten(2)  # (batch_size, embed_dim, n_patches)
        x = x.transpose(1, 2)  # (batch_size, n_patches, embed_dim)
        return x"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Limitations of Standard ViT"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"While vanilla ViT achieves stellar performance on large-scale datasets, it suffers from quadratic computational complexity with respect to image size due to global self-attention. Furthermore, applying standard ViT directly to dense prediction tasks like semantic segmentation or object detection becomes prohibitively expensive for high-resolution images."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Swin Transformer (Shifted Window Transformer) addresses the scalability issue of ViT by constructing hierarchical feature maps and computing self-attention within local, non-overlapping windows. To enable cross-window connections without overlap, it introduces the shifted window partitioning approach."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"6. Key Innovations of Swin Transformer"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Shifted Window Self-Attention: Alternates between standard window partitioning and a shifted configuration to facilitate cross-window information exchange."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Hierarchical Architecture: Merges image patches in deeper layers to construct pyramid feature maps, making it naturally compatible with downstream vision tasks like FPN or U-Net."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Linear Computational Complexity: Complexity scales linearly with image size instead of quadratically, by restricting self-attention to local windows."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"7. Summary and Use Case Selection"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use standard Vision Transformers (ViT) when dealing with image-level classification tasks where global context is paramount and pre-training data is massive. Use Swin Transformers when tackling dense prediction tasks (object detection, segmentation) or handling high-resolution imagery where computational efficiency and hierarchical feature representations are critical."}]
